data.title: U.S. President Donald Trump May Favor Major Iran Operation if Republicans Lose Midterms
data.description: According to Jin10, a U.S. official told Axios that U.S. President Donald Trump may be more inclined to order a large-scale military operation against Iran if Republicans suffer a major defeat in the midterm elections. The official said, “If Trump feels embarrassed or disenfranchised, he will take bold action. Everyone is telling the Iranians that now is the best time to reach a deal.” A White House official said the election results would not affect Trump’s decisions on Iran.

data.title: Crypto Industry Pours More Than $200 Million Into 2026 U.S. Midterm Elections
data.description:
Crypto-related groups have spent more than $200 million in the 2026 U.S. midterm election cycle. According to Sina Finance, citing Public Citizen, crypto groups outspent online gambling and data center development groups in federal corporate political spending during this cycle.

The industry is seeking to repeat its 2024 success, when super PACs spent $250 million to elect pro-crypto lawmakers and reshape Congress. Fairshake and its affiliated super PACs are supporting 33 House candidates—19 Republicans and 14 Democrats—considered key supporters of the industry’s priorities.

The network is prioritizing six House incumbents, providing at least $1 million in seed funding to each of their campaigns. The Republicans include Wisconsin Representative Brian Steil, chair of the House Digital Assets Subcommittee, and Arkansas Representative French Hill and Michigan Representative Bill Huizenga, who are chair and vice chair of the House Financial Services Committee, respectively. Democratic recipients of at least $1 million in Fairshake funding include Oregon Representative Janelle Bynum, California Representative Derek Chen, and Nevada Representative Steven Horsford.

data.title: Iran Studies Proposals in Vance’s Letter, Saudi Broadcaster Reports
data.description: According to Jin10, Saudi broadcaster Al Arabiya reported on October 31, citing sources, that Iran was studying proposals in a letter from U.S. Vice President Vance. The sources said the letter outlined general principles and a framework for negotiations but did not contain a complete proposal. Iran is discussing U.S. proposals concerning its nuclear program. Sources said Iran wants guarantees of a permanent and comprehensive end to hostilities in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iran also insists on a comprehensive ceasefire before negotiations begin. A new round of talks is expected, but it is too early to set a specific date.

data.title: Benton Graham: Stadiums Expand Women's Restroom Capacity as Women's Sports Grow
data.description: Writer and journalist Benton Graham said newer stadiums and arenas are dedicating more restroom capacity to women as women's sports grow, according to Bloomberg. Equal restroom space does not necessarily mean equal access, he said, while upgrades at older stadiums can carry significant costs.

data.title: zkLink Attack Exploits Transient Storage Vulnerability, Causing $783,000 Loss
data.description: Cross-chain protocol zkLink was attacked on October 29, resulting in losses of about $783,000. According to Odaily, the SlowMist security team said the attacker exploited a residual validation value in transient storage to forge a batch root used to verify withdrawals. The attacker made 12 withdrawals: one in ETH and 11 in ERC-20 tokens. The attacker first claimed a genuine cross-chain message to write the validation value, then reused it in a later call within the same transaction to forge the batch root through relay and gateway contracts. The contracts allowed relayers to specify external call targets and parameters, while the validation value was neither cleared nor bound to the current call; batch-root updates checked only the gateway’s identity and did not require independent proof verification.

data.title: Iran's Foreign Minister: No Current Plans to Meet U.S. Officials
data.description: According to Jin10, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on October 31 that Iran had no current plans to meet U.S. officials and that speculation about a meeting was media hype. Araghchi said U.S. Vice President Vance's letter had been carefully reviewed and discussed at a high-level Iranian meeting. He praised U.S. efforts to create more room for dialogue and understanding, calling them a positive step, but said the United States would be making a new mistake if the letter was intended to divide Iran. Araghchi said Iran saw no need to meet with the United States, its conditions were clear, and mediators were continuing discussions on them. If the United States agreed to Iran's conditions, Iran would decide whether negotiations would be direct or indirect. He also said an Iranian delegation had gone to Doha and Iran's deputy foreign minister was continuing consultations on the conditions in Qatar.

data.title: Tom Lee Thinks Forced Selling May Be Behind Nasdaq’s Stock Crash
data.description: Tom Lee said a large investor may have been forced to dump tech shares, as the Nasdaq Composite posted its worst month since March 2025, down 5.3%, and its worst day since June 5; Intel fell 28.6% after weak fourth-quarter guidance. The equal-weight S&P 500 rose as Lee spoke but closed down 0.79%, versus a 1.82% drop for the regular index, according to BeInCrypto. Lee said investors are waiting until November 3rd’s midterm elections; the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.93%, and CME FedWatch put December rate-hike odds at 72%. Amazon reported $42.4 billion in negative free cash flow, driven by heavy AI spending.

data.title: An Address Earned About $25.36 Million in 30 Days and Cut Its BTC Short by $11.94 Million
data.description: An address recorded about $25.36 million in account gains over the past 30 days and reduced its BTC short position by about $11.94 million. According to Odaily, the address still holds short positions totaling about 79.69 BTC, valued at approximately $6.17 million. It closed about $11.92 million in BTC shorts during the period at an average execution price of $77,362.13. The address, 0xdd53c5297309130ab5fe5623dc905752e3342b13, has total losses of about $18.79 million.

data.title: Automatic 401(k) Rollovers Cut Cash-Outs, but Few Reach New Employer Plans, Research Finds
data.description: According to CNBC, Vanguard research found that automatic 401(k) rollovers reduced cash-outs among workers leaving jobs, but only 6% of accounts transferred to interim IRAs had reached a new employer plan as of early 2026. Among workers with balances below $1,000, the share who cashed out within 10 months fell to about 9% from roughly 50% after their employers joined the Portability Services Network. For balances of $1,000 to $7,000, the share fell to 31% from 39%. The network generally moves small balances into safe harbor IRAs and then into a new employer’s 401(k) if that employer also participates; few employers have opted in. Since its November 2023 launch, the network has completed 53,118 transfers totaling $71.3 million, according to Steve Holman of Retirement Clearinghouse.

data.title: Haunted Attractions Bring Visitors and Investment to Urban Neighborhoods
data.description: Haunted attractions are drawing visitors and investment to struggling neighborhoods, including Baltimore’s Old Town and former industrial districts in Kansas City and Salt Lake City, according to Bloomberg. Journalist Elizabeth Yuko said operators can support urban revitalization by investing in infrastructure, attracting businesses and finding new uses for neglected properties.

data.title: Iran's Foreign Minister: Iran Will Persist and Resist, Relying on Its Own Capabilities to Overcome This Difficult Period
data.description: According to Jin10, Iran's foreign minister said Iran will continue to persevere and resist, and will overcome this difficult period through its own capabilities.

data.title: CertiK: Crypto Industry Losses Hit Record $9.2 Billion in 2026
data.description: CertiK's live data dashboard shows cumulative crypto industry losses reached a record $9.2 billion in 2026. According to ChainCatcher, $3.03 billion in assets were frozen or recovered in October, bringing adjusted losses for the month to $3.47 billion.

data.title: Uniswap TJAR Fee Conversion System Opens to All Apps and Covers Seven Chains
data.description: Uniswap said on X that its TJAR fee conversion system is now available to all applications. According to Odaily, the system lets applications convert fees received in different tokens into a designated token. It processed more than $15.3 million in conversions last month and now operates across seven chains. Robinhood uses TJAR through the Uniswap API and receives fees in USDC and USDG.

data.title: AI | AI Enthusiasm Slumps as Tech Earnings Add to Market Concerns
data.description: AI enthusiasm is collapsing, and technology earnings have added to concerns weighing on a stock market facing doubts about heavy artificial-intelligence spending, according to Bloomberg. A series of technology giants reported earnings over the last two weeks, a period that was expected to bring clarity.

data.title: Iran's Foreign Minister: Iran Demands an End to the War on All Fronts, Including Lebanon
data.description: According to Jin10, Iran's foreign minister said Iran demands an end to the war on all fronts, including the Lebanon front.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Kaja Kallas Warns Against Normalizing Russia Internationally
data.description:
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Russia is escalating its war in Ukraine and is not serious about peace, criticizing Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov’s remarks at the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta, according to Bloomberg. Kallas warned against normalizing Moscow on the international stage.

In an interview with Bloomberg This Weekend host David Gura, Kallas also called for a diplomatic solution to tensions with Iran and discussed deepening the EU’s relationship with Canada through increased cooperation on trade, energy and defense.

data.title: Iran's Foreign Minister: No Possibility of War Is Ruled Out, Forces at Highest Readiness
data.description: According to Jin10, Iran's foreign minister said Iran does not rule out any possibility of war breaking out and is prepared for all scenarios, having upgraded its weapons and equipment, addressed weaknesses, tested new weapons, and placed its troops at the highest state of readiness.

data.title: Iran's Foreign Minister: Iran Is a Party to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and Fulfills Its Obligations
data.description: According to Jin10, Iran's foreign minister said Iran is a party to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons and complies with its obligations under the treaty.

data.title: Senegal Parliament Again Rejects Budget, Threatening IMF Program Approval
data.description: Senegalese lawmakers again rejected the government’s revised 2026 finance law, prolonging a standoff that threatens to delay approval of an International Monetary Fund program, according to Bloomberg.

data.description: According to Jin10, Iran's foreign minister thanked Qatar and Pakistan for their efforts and continued communication.
